subtopic: Static shape specialization / Dynamic vs. symbolic shape
learningObjective: Reason about the trade-offs of static shape specialization versus symbolic-shape (dynamic) compilation at the graph-IR level.

softwareContext.framework: TVM Relax / TorchInductor / general graph IR

options.text: Because the specialized function has concrete shapes, it is a strict semantic superset of the symbolic version and can substitute for `f` in every call site, since concrete shape info can always be relaxed back to symbolic at will.

Static-shape specialization is a naming convenience only; it does not affect emitted kernel selection or downstream optimizations, because tiling and vectorization operate on abstract loop nests that ignore the concrete shape metadata.

Shape specialization enables downstream passes (tiling, kernel selection, constant folding of shape-derived quantities) to produce a more efficient kernel at the cost of covering only one input-shape configuration.

After specialization, calling `f_32x4096x4096` on inputs with shape `[64, 4096]` silently returns correct but slower results because the compiler installs a runtime dispatch to the symbolic implementation.

explanation: Shape specialization narrows the input domain (the specialized version accepts only one shape configuration) in exchange for compile-time knowledge that enables tile-size selection, static memory planning, constant-folded index arithmetic, and shape-specific kernel dispatch. The trade-off is compilation cost and possible cache blow-up if many shape configurations need coverage.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: specialization narrows the domain (subset), not a superset. Substituting for `f` in general call sites where shapes differ would be a type/shape error.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: downstream passes make shape-dependent choices (tiling factors, kernel templates, vectorization width). Removing symbolic dimensions materially changes emitted code.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: this captures both the benefit and the cost of specialization accurately.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: shape mismatch at the specialized function's boundary produces an error or verifier failure, not a silent slower path.

assumptions: The graph IR verifier enforces static shape compatibility at boundaries.
There is a downstream tiling/kernel-selection pass that uses static shape information.
nonImplications: Does not imply that dynamic shape support is inferior in general; symbolic shapes reduce compile cache size and warm-up time.
Does not imply that a specialized kernel is always faster; if the specialization mismatches actual runtime shapes and forces re-compilation, throughput can be worse.
